"FATEBEARER is a 2D Pixel Art Historical Fantasy Grand Strategy Game set in a fictional world inspired by three great civilizations: Europe, Asia, and Africa. Rather than using 3D graphics, Fatebearer features a lightweight 2D pixel art visual style, presenting its world through a detailed interactive map where players can observe kingdoms, territories, castles, capitals, borders, alliances, and ongoing conflicts. Each civilization has its own unique culture, architecture, military units, equipment, royal traditions, and visual identity inspired by historical kingdoms and dynasties. Players begin their journey as a military recruit serving a kingdom, choosing a male or female character, creating their own first name and family surname, and gradually rising through military ranks until they become a Royal General, Supreme Commander, Warlord, or even an Emperor. The player's family surname will eventually become the identity of a powerful dynasty passed down through generations. Players can recruit, train, upgrade, and command various military units, including infantry, elite guards, archers, cavalry, knights, and siege weapons such as ballistae, trebuchets, battering rams, and siege towers, while advanced weapons such as cannons become available through technological progression. Warfare is presented through animated 2D pixel art battles, where armies visibly fight against each other, archers release volleys of arrows, cavalry charge across the battlefield, infantry clash, and siege engines attack enemy fortifications. Battles are influenced by troop numbers, military experience, morale, equipment, technology, generals, and strategic decisions. Players can declare wars, defend their territories, conquer castles, capture trade cities, establish alliances, negotiate peace treaties, and expand their influence across multiple continents. Every conquered castle can be renamed and customized with the player's dynasty name, banners, flags, emblems, colors, and architectural styles, allowing each territory to reflect the identity of its new ruler. Capturing land is not simply about military victory, as players must also manage their territories, appoint governors, collect taxes, develop economies, construct military academies, royal palaces, treasuries, markets, blacksmiths, and royal archives, while maintaining the loyalty of their populations. Beyond military power, Fatebearer features a deep political system in which players can serve their king loyally, gain influence within the Royal Council, form alliances with powerful nobles, challenge royal decisions, or face betrayal when their growing popularity becomes a threat to the throne. Players may eventually rebel against their kingdom, declare independence, overthrow the monarch, establish their own empire, or claim the imperial throne. Conquering 100 castles becomes a major milestone that grants the player an opportunity to challenge the ruling kingdom and pursue supreme power, although maintaining those territories remains just as important as conquering them. The world continues to evolve independently through an advanced AI kingdom system, where rival kingdoms can wage wars, form alliances, experience economic crises, change rulers, expand their borders, lose territories, and collapse without the player's involvement. Fatebearer also introduces a dynasty and family system, allowing players to marry through royal arranged marriages or meet potential partners while exploring cities, castles, and territories affected by war. Their partners have individual backgrounds and personalities, while their children inherit the family surname and develop unique traits, talents, abilities, and ambitions. Players can influence their children's education through military, political, economic, or diplomatic paths, preparing them for the future of the dynasty. When the main character eventually dies of old age, the player continues the journey through their descendants, facing inheritance disputes

- Build and refine a complete, playable Fatebearer historical-fantasy grand strategy game in the existing project.
- Continue reviewing gameplay and responsive visuals, with JPEG screenshots captured at viewport widths no greater than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Implement a playable world map, military progression and battles, realm management, politics, dynasty, and succession.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at widths no greater than 1280px.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a self-contained browser experience in `index.html`, with inline CSS, SVG map art, JavaScript, and localStorage saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented character creation, seasonal turns, resources, recruitment and training, sieges and battles, territorial ownership, realm investments, council petitions, dynasty marriage and children, succession, and AI events.

- Build and refine a complete, playable Fatebearer historical-fantasy grand strategy game in the existing project.
- Continue reviewing gameplay and responsive visuals, with JPEG screenshots captured at viewport widths no greater than 1280px.
